Let \(N_m\) be the required number. The answer is

\[
\boxed{
N_m=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{160\cdot 2^{3m}-42\cdot 2^{2m}-55}{63},& m\ \text{even},\\[6pt]
\dfrac{160\cdot 2^{3m}-84\cdot 2^{2m}+1}{63},& m\ \text{odd}.
\end{cases}}
\]

**Solution.**

Write \(R=\mathbb Z/2^m\mathbb Z\), and use the symplectic basis
\[
e_1,e_2,f_1,f_2
\]
where \(\langle e_i,f_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}\) and all other pairings among basis vectors vanish.

If \(H=H^\perp\), then
\[
|H|\,|H^\perp|=|G|=2^{4m},
\]
so \(|H|=2^{2m}\), and \(H\) is maximal isotropic.

A standard symplectic Smith normal form applies over the principal ideal ring \(R\): every maximal isotropic subgroup is carried by an element of \(\operatorname{Sp}_4(R)\) to exactly one subgroup of the form

\[
H_{a,b}
=
\langle
2^a e_1,\,
2^b e_2,\,
2^{m-a} f_1,\,
2^{m-b} f_2
\rangle,
\]
with
\[
0\le a\le b\le \left\lfloor \frac m2\right\rfloor .
\]

Indeed, the displayed subgroup is isotropic because each \(e_i\)-\(f_i\) pairing is multiplied by \(2^m\), and it has order
\[
2^{m-a}2^{m-b}2^a2^b=2^{2m},
\]
so it is self-orthogonal of the correct size, hence self-dual. Conversely, symplectic row-column reduction gives this form, and the ordered pair \((a,b)\) is determined by the elementary divisor data of \(H\).

It remains to count the orbit of each \(H_{a,b}\). Put
\[
u=\frac m2-a,\qquad v=\frac m2-b,
\]
so \(u\ge v\ge0\). The stabilizer calculation in \(\operatorname{Sp}_4(R)\) gives the following orbit sizes.

If \(m\) is even, so \(u,v\in\mathbb Z\), then
\[
|{\mathcal O}_{u,v}|=
\begin{cases}
1,&(u,v)=(0,0),\\
15\cdot 2^{4u-3},&u>0,\ v=0,\\
15\cdot 2^{4u+2v-3},&u\ge v>0.
\end{cases}
\]

If \(m\) is odd, then \(u,v\in \mathbb Z+\tfrac12\), and always \(v>0\), with
\[
|{\mathcal O}_{u,v}|=15\cdot 2^{4u+2v-3}.
\]

For even \(m=2c\), summing over \(c\ge u\ge v\ge0\) gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
N_{2c}
&=1+\frac{15}{8}\sum_{u=1}^c 2^{4u}\left(1+\sum_{v=1}^u2^{2v}\right)\\
&=1+\frac{15}{8}\sum_{u=1}^c 16^u\cdot \frac{4^{u+1}-1}{3}\\
&=\frac{160\cdot 2^{6c}-42\cdot 2^{4c}-55}{63}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(m=2c\), this is
\[
N_m=\frac{160\cdot 2^{3m}-42\cdot 2^{2m}-55}{63}.
\]

For odd \(m=2c+1\), write
\[
u=i+\frac12,\qquad v=j+\frac12,
\]
where \(0\le j\le i\le c\). Then
\[
\begin{aligned}
N_{2c+1}
&=\sum_{i=0}^c\sum_{j=0}^i 15\cdot 2^{4i+2j}\\
=15\sum_{i=0}^c16^i\sum_{j=0}^i4^j\\
&=5\sum_{i=0}^c16^i(4^{i+1}-1)\\
&=\frac{20\cdot 64^{c+1}-21\cdot 16^{c+1}+1}{63}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(m=2c+1\), this becomes
\[
N_m=\frac{160\cdot 2^{3m}-84\cdot 2^{2m}+1}{63}.
\]

As checks: for \(m=1\), this gives \(15\), the number of Lagrangian planes in \(\mathbb F_2^4\); for \(m=2\), it gives \(151\). Thus the required number is

\[
\boxed{
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{160\cdot 2^{3m}-42\cdot 2^{2m}-55}{63},& m\ \mathrm{even},\\[6pt]
\dfrac{160\cdot 2^{3m}-84\cdot 2^{2m}+1}{63},& m\ \mathrm{odd}.
\end{cases}}
\]
